While reporting in the eastern city of Kramatorsk, journalists for the state-funded television channel Freedom TV, Olena Hubanova (known by her pseudonym Alyona Hramova) and Yevhen Karmazin, are killed by a Russian drone strike on their car while working nearby. Their colleague Oleksandr Kolychev is seriously injured and taken to hospital.

The television tower in Chernihiv, a city in northern Ukraine, is damaged following a Russian strike on the city.

While reporting in the village of Rodynske, north-east of the city of Pokrovsk in the Donetsk region, Andriy Kramchenkov, editor-in-chief of the Donbass branch of the public broadcaster Suspilne, and his colleague Vladyslav Ukolov are targeted by a Russian drone. The journalists, equipped with black bulletproof vests marked “press,” manage to take cover and emerge unharmed.

A drone attack targeting the eastern city of Dnipro strikes the premises of the public broadcaster Suspilne in the evening. The Dnipro television tower is hit during the attack, causing a break in broadcasting for several hours. The offices of the Ukrainian organisation Institute of Mass Information (IMI) is also damaged.

A Russian FPV (first-person view) drone strikes an evacuation vehicle near Lyman, in the Donetsk region, in which Serhiy Horbatenko, a journalist with Donbass Realii – a local project of Radio Svoboda, the Ukrainian branch of Radio Free Europe/Radio Liberty – was reporting. He escaped with a concussion.

While reporting with the Ukrainian army near the town of Dobropillia, in the Donetsk region of eastern Ukraine, French editor-in-chief of the media outlet Défense Zone Fred Marie and French photographer David Taché, both members of the Collectif DR, along with their Ukrainian fixer Rostyslav Tsyren, come under attack from a Russian FPV (first-person view, immersively piloted) drone targeting the Ukrainian army vehicle transporting them.
